PDF.js vendor provenance — InkDOS PDF workspace

Upstream project: Mozilla PDF.js (https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js)
Vendored display/runtime version: 6.4.299
Package: pdfjs-dist 6.4.299, legacy build (broader WebView support for the desktop hosts)
npm integrity: sha512-AVl138zALtfaAPvADulE0PZThbYzCBS79nL4pOSL/6Sm/4AH5A21BD9VHt97OlCuzJuCpmeZtAtkinisF4Vb1g==
License: Apache License 2.0 (LICENSE-PDFJS.txt; decoder licenses in wasm/)

Reproduce: npm pack pdfjs-dist@6.4.299, then
  python scripts/vendor_pdfjs.py pdfjs-dist-6.4.299.tgz          (write)
  python scripts/vendor_pdfjs.py pdfjs-dist-6.4.299.tgz --check  (verify)
The script checks the tarball against the npm integrity above and applies the worker patch.

Files:
- pdf.min.mjs: upstream legacy/build/pdf.min.mjs, unmodified. SHA-256 bccc24ea711db8e44503629519904a5292d73b9daaa214bbe7cdcc282b0f4259
- pdf.worker.min.mjs: upstream legacy/build/pdf.worker.min.mjs with the InkDOS patch.
  SHA-256 9ddd2c36b87cbb3319ac7ea354c0f396f344a06c8b6f8e3037e5e92ec5f005a4
- wasm/: upstream image decoders (OpenJPEG for JPEG 2000, JBIG2) with their pure-JS fallbacks, and
  QCMS for ICC colors, unmodified. Fetched from this origin through the getDocument wasmUrl option.

Worker patch (only change to PDF.js): AnnotationFactory.saveNewAnnotations writes the InkDOS review
records kept in AnnotationStorage by apps/pdf/extensions/review-annotations.js (types 1109 Highlight,
1110 Underline, 1101 Text) as standard PDF markup annotations, so saveDocument() keeps them in the
incremental update. The types sit outside PDF.js's own editor type range (101 is SIGNATURE in 6.x).
The 3.11.174 "structural only" save switch was not carried over: no InkDOS code used it.

Loading: PDF.js 6 is an ES module. apps/pdf/pdfjs/pdfjs-global.mjs publishes it as the pdfjsLib
global; the workspace scripts load with `defer` after it. There is no remote/CDN dependency and one
PDF.js worker at runtime.
